transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello. Well... I suppose I'm here because I've been spending rather a lot of my day checking on things. 

Just... opening my drawers and folders, and some labeled boxes I keep. I keep opening them to make sure my important papers and keepsakes are still exactly where I left them. Even if I just looked a few minutes before, I... I end up doing it again and again. It's taking up too much of my time, I suppose.
What goes through your mind when you think about not checking on these things?

Well... it's just a thought that keeps needling me, really. Even when I know better. 

I just... I start worrying that perhaps I've accidentally thrown away my husband's old tax papers. Or... or maybe I put a family recipe in the wrong box. If I try not to go look, I just... I can't seem to let it pass. I start feeling like I've done something terribly careless. So I have to check.
Do you feel the need to perform any specific physical actions, like cleaning or arranging things, over and over?
No... I don't believe so. I keep a tidy house, but I don't clean things repeatedly or... or rearrange them. It's really just what I've already told you.
Do you worry that something bad might happen if you don't check on these things?
No... I don't believe so. I don't think about any sort of catastrophe happening, if that's what you mean. I just... well, I just don't want things to be lost. That's really all there is to it.
Do you feel like the things you're checking need to be in a specific order or arrangement for you to feel okay about not checking them again?
No, I... I don't think so. I just need to see that they're there. I don't need to line them up or... or put them in any particular order. Just knowing they haven't been thrown out is enough.
Do you feel like you're checking to make sure you haven't made a mistake?

Well... I suppose so. Yes. It's just... even when I know better, a thought will just keep needling me. I'll start worrying that I might have accidentally thrown away my husband's old tax papers, or... or maybe put a family recipe in the wrong box. I just can't seem to let it pass without feeling like I've done something terribly careless. So... yes, I suppose I am checking for that.
Do you worry that you might forget where you put something if you don't check on it?
No, not really. I... I know where I put them. I just need to make sure they're still there.
Do you feel like you would be to blame if something were to happen to one of these important papers or keepsakes?
I... I'm not really sure. I haven't thought about it like that. I just... I just wouldn't want them to be gone. That's all.
Do you feel like you would be responsible if one of your important papers or keepsakes were to be lost?
I... well, I suppose that's what we were just saying. I don't really look at it as... being responsible. I just know I wouldn't want them to go missing.
Do you think your checking would stop if you were absolutely certain you hadn't made a mistake when putting something away?
I... I really couldn't say. I haven't thought about it like that. I just... I just check on them.
Do you think you would still feel the need to check on these things if someone you trust confirmed that everything is in its correct place?
I... I don't know if that would make a difference, to be honest. I just prefer to see them with my own eyes. I haven't really had anyone else do it, so... I couldn't say.
Do you think you would still feel the need to check on these things if you were completely confident that you had put them away correctly?
I... well, I thought you just asked me something like that. I really couldn't tell you. I don't... I don't really think about being completely confident or anything like that. I just check on them.
Do you think the need to check on these things would go away if you were absolutely certain that you hadn't made a mistake when putting them away?
I... Doctor, we've gone over this. I just... I don't know how else to answer. I check them. That's all I know.
Do you think the idea of making a mistake is what's driving you to check on these things?

I suppose it could be. It's just... even when I know better, a thought will just start needling me. Like... maybe I threw away my husband's old tax papers by accident, or put a family recipe in the wrong box. I just get this feeling that I've done something terribly careless, and... I can't seem to let it pass.
Is the feeling that you've made a mistake what's causing you to go check on these things again?

I suppose it is. I just... I can't shake it. That's why I'm here, really. I just spend so much of my day... opening the same folders, the same drawers. Looking in those labeled boxes again and again. Just to make sure the important papers and the keepsakes are still where I left them. Even if I just checked them a few minutes ago. I just... have to look again.
Is it the possibility of having made a mistake that bothers you, or is it more about needing to know that everything is exactly as it should be?
I... I really couldn't say. I don't sit and analyze it like that. I just... I just know I have to go look. I'm not sure there's much of a difference to me.
Is it the thought of possibly having made a mistake that's driving you to check, rather than just wanting to be certain everything is in its place?
I don't... I don't know. Like I said, I don't really pull it apart like that. It's just a feeling that I have to go check. I'm not sure it matters why.
Is the feeling that you need to make sure everything is correct what's driving you to check, rather than the fear of having made a mistake?
I... I really don't know how else to explain it to you. It's just... I just have to check. I don't know which one it is.
Is your need to check on these things more about avoiding the feeling of having made a mistake or about feeling certain that everything is in its place?
I... I feel like you keep asking me the exact same thing. And I... I really still don't have a different answer for you. I just don't know. I just do it.
Is the possibility of having made a mistake the main reason you feel like you need to check on these things?
I... I don't know what else to say. I've told you, I just don't know. I just check. That's all.
